questions.question: When do you need an air brake endorsement?

options.text: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.
To transport hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You need to pass an air brakes test to drive a vehicle with air brakes. This includes vehicles with air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The nuts are loose.
The nuts are wet.
The nuts need to be replaced.
The nuts are the wrong size.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts often means they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust.

questions.question: When turning to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
Turn the wheel very sharply.
Hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it can lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning. Braking during a turn can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: What can cause poisonous fumes to enter the cab?

options.text: A broken exhaust system.
Using the wrong type of fuel.
Low oil in the engine.
Under-inflated tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: When avoiding a hazard, which is more effective?

options.text: Stopping is always effective.
Swerving may work better than stopping.
You can change lanes without looking.
You should drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than stopping.
questions.explanation: You can usually turn away from a hazard faster than you can stop completely. However, swerving can cause a rollover in top-heavy vehicles or vehicles pulling multiple trailers.

questions.question: What should you do before adding coolant to a system without a recovery tank?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Open the radiator cap quickly.
Do not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Turn off the engine and let it cool first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine and let it cool first.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and wait for it to cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them the same way every time.
Check different items each time.
You can check items in a different order each time.
You do not need to check every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way. This helps you remember all the important things to check.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?

options.text: Before you enter the curve.
While you are in the curve.
After you exit the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause a skid.

questions.question: How can a driver test the coupling?

options.text: By placing their fingers inside the coupling mechanism.
By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
By placing glue over the fifth wheel.
By releasing the orange lever in the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer coupling before starting a trip. For double or triple combinations, test by pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.

questions.question: What happens when you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake drum tightens onto the axle.
The brake lining presses against the wheel.
Air is released from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, it pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be:

options.text: Checked for leaks.
Securely connected to the battery.
Carrying fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Simpler than driving during the day.
Discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare affects your vision, and more tired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Get upset.
Stay calm and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. Take a deep breath and accept that you will be late. Safe driving is more important than being on time.

questions.question: To avoid slowing traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Switch gears while driving uphill.
Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane when possible.
questions.explanation: If your truck cannot keep up with traffic speed because of a heavy load, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So that it must be backed up to leave.
So that it can be pulled forward to leave.
On the grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that it can be pulled forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
Get upset.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: To avoid dangerous and aggressive driving, relax and accept delays. Plan for extra time when you know traffic might be heavy.

questions.question: Retreaded tires:

options.text: May be used on any part of a bus.
May be used on the front of a bus.
May be used on the rear of a bus.
May never be used on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be used on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that measures liquid in the air brake system.
A valve that releases excess pressure from the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar, also called the trailer hand valve or trolley valve, controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, the safety latch or lock should be:

options.text: Engaged.
Deactivated.
Polished.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engaged.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the fifth wheel, make sure the release arm is seated properly and the safety latch or lock is engaged. All parts should be present and working correctly.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking capacity.
Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with a vehicle's normal braking system and does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when the wheels are about to lock.
